fields.description:
KIP-1071 defines the error code STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH (131) for a member that sends a topology that doesn't match the group's topology at the same epoch. The error code and StreamsInvalidTopologyEpochException exist, and StreamsGroupHeartbeatResponse lists the error as supported, but the group coordinator never returns it.

In GroupMetadataManager#maybeUpdateTopology, when the group already has a topology and the request carries a topology with an equal or higher epoch that differs from the stored one, the coordinator throws InvalidRequestException("Topology updates are not supported yet."). The same-epoch case should return STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH. It means two instances of the application are running different topologies under the same epoch, and a specific error helps users diagnose it. The higher-epoch case is an actual topology update, which is not yet supported, and can keep returning INVALID_REQUEST.

The KIP-1331 topology description push has the same problem. GroupMetadataManager#validateStreamsGroupTopologyDescriptionUpdate throws InvalidRequestException when the pushed epoch doesn't match the group's current topology epoch. It should throw StreamsInvalidTopologyEpochException, and StreamsGroupTopologyDescriptionUpdateResponse.json should list STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH among its supported errors. The mismatch can happen in normal operation, when the epoch is bumped between the heartbeat that requested the push and the push itself. So the client should log it below warn level.

Clients need no protocol changes and behave the same way. StreamsGroupHeartbeatRequestManager already treats STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH as fatal, just like INVALID_REQUEST. StreamsGroupTopologyDescriptionRequestManager handles it in its default branch, which drops the push without retrying, the same as for INVALID_REQUEST; we should add an explicit case there. GroupCoordinatorService already maps the exception to code 131 through Errors.forException.
fields.summary: Return STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH instead of INVALID_REQUEST for topology epoch mismatches in streams groups

fields.description:
h3. Problem

KAFKA-19682 (#20693, first released in 4.2.0) added a log message to {{{}PartitionGroup#readyToProcess{}}}. The method returns this message in {{{}ReadyToProcessResult{}}}. It builds the message with {{String.format}} and a {{StringBuilder}} for each partition that has no buffered records:
{code:java}
final Long fetchedLag = fetchedLags.getOrDefault(partition, -1L);
appendLog(logMessageBuilder, String.format("Partition %s has fetched lag of %d", partition, fetchedLag));
...
appendLog(logMessageBuilder,
    String.format("Partition %s has current lag %d, but no data is buffered locally. Waiting to buffer some records.",
    partition, fetchedLag));
...
appendLog(logMessageBuilder, String.format(
    "Partition %s has current lag 0 and current time is %d. " +
        "Waiting for new data to be produced for configured idle time %d (deadline is %d).",
    partition, wallClockTime, maxTaskIdleMs, deadline));
{code}
No log-level check protects this code. It runs each time {{StreamTask#isProcessable}} calls {{{}readyToProcess{}}}, and the {{TaskExecutor}} loop does this {*}for each record{*}. The code runs when a task has more than one input partition and at least one of those partitions has no buffered records. This is a normal condition for a task that reads a low-volume topic together with a high-volume topic.

The caller then discards almost every message:
 * {{StreamTask#isProcessable}} discards the message when the task changes from READY to NOT_READY ({{{}wasReady{}}}).
 * {{StreamTask#maybeLogNotReady}} logs the message at INFO only when {{NOT_READY_LOG_INTERVAL_MS}} (120 s) passed since the last log. It discards all other messages.
 * When a partition reaches its idle deadline and the task becomes ready ({{{}enforced{}}}), the method returns {{{}ReadyToProcessResult(true, Optional.empty()){}}}. It discards the "has fetched lag" text that it already formatted for that partition.

Before 4.2.0, this method logged the same states with {{{}logger.trace("...{}...", ...){}}}. That code formatted no text when TRACE was disabled.
h3. Impact

We upgraded a Kafka Streams application from 3.8 to 4.4.0. The application runs EOS v2 and has several sub-topologies with more than one input partition for each task.

We recorded a 5-minute JFR profile on one instance during the catch-up after a restart. In this profile:
 * {{PartitionGroup#readyToProcess}} is 19.7% of the StreamThread CPU samples. {{String.format}} called from it is 15.1%, and this includes {{DecimalFormatSymbols.<init>}} and {{{}Formatter.parse{}}}.
 * {{ArrayList}} allocations from {{Formatter.parse}} are 13.7% of the sampled allocation weight.

The 3.8 profile of the same application has no equivalent cost.
h3. Proposed fix

Do not build the message unless the caller will log it. Possible approaches:
 # Return the not-ready reason as structured data in {{{}ReadyToProcessResult{}}}: the partition, the fetched lag, the deadline and the reason. Let {{StreamTask#maybeLogNotReady}} format the text only when it logs.
 # Alternatively, make {{readyToProcess}} build the message only when the caller asks for it. For example, pass a flag that {{StreamTask}} sets when {{NOT_READY_LOG_INTERVAL_MS}} passed.

Both approaches keep the log output of KAFKA-19682 and remove the cost from the processing loop.
h3. Workaround

{{max.task.idle.ms=-1}} makes {{readyToProcess}} return before the loop. But this setting also disables the wait for unfetched data, so a task can process records out of order. It is not a safe workaround for applications that need the default behaviour.

renderedFields.description:
Problem

KAFKA-19682 (#20693, first released in 4.2.0) added a log message to PartitionGroup#readyToProcess. The method returns this message in ReadyToProcessResult. It builds the message with String.format and a StringBuilder for each partition that has no buffered records:

final Long fetchedLag = fetchedLags.getOrDefault(partition, -1L);
appendLog(logMessageBuilder, String.format("Partition %s has fetched lag of %d", partition, fetchedLag));
...
appendLog(logMessageBuilder,
    String.format("Partition %s has current lag %d, but no data is buffered locally. Waiting to buffer some records.",
    partition, fetchedLag));
...
appendLog(logMessageBuilder, String.format(
    "Partition %s has current lag 0 and current time is %d. " +
        "Waiting for new data to be produced for configured idle time %d (deadline is %d).",
    partition, wallClockTime, maxTaskIdleMs, deadline));

No log-level check protects this code. It runs each time StreamTask#isProcessable calls readyToProcess, and the TaskExecutor loop does this for each record. The code runs when a task has more than one input partition and at least one of those partitions has no buffered records. This is a normal condition for a task that reads a low-volume topic together with a high-volume topic.

The caller then discards almost every message:

  • StreamTask#isProcessable discards the message when the task changes from READY to NOT_READY (wasReady).
  • StreamTask#maybeLogNotReady logs the message at INFO only when NOT_READY_LOG_INTERVAL_MS (120 s) passed since the last log. It discards all other messages.
  • When a partition reaches its idle deadline and the task becomes ready (enforced), the method returns ReadyToProcessResult(true, Optional.empty()). It discards the "has fetched lag" text that it already formatted for that partition.

Before 4.2.0, this method logged the same states with logger.trace("...{}...", ...). That code formatted no text when TRACE was disabled.

Impact

We upgraded a Kafka Streams application from 3.8 to 4.4.0. The application runs EOS v2 and has several sub-topologies with more than one input partition for each task.

We recorded a 5-minute JFR profile on one instance during the catch-up after a restart. In this profile:

  • PartitionGroup#readyToProcess is 19.7% of the StreamThread CPU samples. String.format called from it is 15.1%, and this includes DecimalFormatSymbols.<init> and Formatter.parse.
  • ArrayList allocations from Formatter.parse are 13.7% of the sampled allocation weight.

The 3.8 profile of the same application has no equivalent cost.

Proposed fix

Do not build the message unless the caller will log it. Possible approaches:

  1. Return the not-ready reason as structured data in ReadyToProcessResult: the partition, the fetched lag, the deadline and the reason. Let StreamTask#maybeLogNotReady format the text only when it logs.
  2. Alternatively, make readyToProcess build the message only when the caller asks for it. For example, pass a flag that StreamTask sets when NOT_READY_LOG_INTERVAL_MS passed.

Both approaches keep the log output of KAFKA-19682 and remove the cost from the processing loop.

Workaround

max.task.idle.ms=-1 makes readyToProcess return before the loop. But this setting also disables the wait for unfetched data, so a task can process records out of order. It is not a safe workaround for applications that need the default behaviour.

fields.summary: Streams: reads of a global store pass the headers of the global thread's last record to the value deserializer

comments.body:
The PR covers both: it resets the record context + returns empty headers to readers other than the global thread.

One related gap: StreamTask never resets its record context either, so an IQ on a task store still gets the task's last processed record headers (same regression from KAFKA-20173). Fix here or separate ticket?

renderedFields.description:
Since KAFKA-20173 the metered stores pass internalContext.headers() to the serdes. For a global store that context is the global processor context, so every read of a global store gives the value deserializer the headers of the last record the global thread processed:
-> a processor in a stream task that reads a global store gets the global thread's last record headers, not the headers of the record it is processing. A task store read in the same processor gets the right ones.
-> an interactive query on a global store gets them too, while the comment in MeteredKeyValueStore (511-513, 534-536) says the IQ path gets new RecordHeaders() since there is no record context.

4.2.1 passed no headers on these reads. Line numbers below are at 4.3.2, the same code is in 4.4.0 and on trunk (not run on trunk).

Why:
-> GlobalStateManagerImpl.initialize inits every global store with globalProcessorContext (189).
-> ProcessorContextImpl.getStateStore gives a stream task the same store instance, read only (167-170).
-> MeteredKeyValueStore keeps that context from init (135) and passes internalContext.headers() to the serdes on get and put (449-461).
-> GlobalStateUpdateTask.update sets the record context for each record (115-122) and nothing resets it.

So what a stream thread's read gets depends on how far the global thread has got. That record context is written by the global thread and read by the stream threads without any synchronization.

It matters for value serdes that look at headers. Confluent's Avro deserializer for example, by default (DualSchemaIdDeserializer in 8.2.2 and 8.3.0), takes the schema id from a __value_schema_id header when there is one and then reads the whole value as the payload. A global store value stored with the id in its prefix is then decoded with another record's schema id whenever the global thread's last record carried that header.

Repro: TopologyTestDriver, in-memory stores, a value deserializer that records the "origin" header it is given. A global record with origin=global-record is piped first, then a stream record with origin=stream-record whose processor reads a task store and the global store, then an interactive query on the global store.

Results:

Read 4.2.1 4.3.2 4.4.0
task store read in the stream task processor called without headers origin=stream-record origin=stream-record
global store read in the same processor called without headers origin=global-record origin=global-record
interactive query on the global store called without headers origin=global-record origin=global-record

TopologyTestDriver runs the global and the stream processing on one thread. I also saw it on 4.3.2 with KafkaStreams against a real broker in one of our integration tests, where the global thread is its own thread.

import org.apache.kafka.common.header.Headers;
import org.apache.kafka.common.header.internals.RecordHeaders;
import org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.Deserializer;
import org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.Serde;
import org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.Serdes;
import org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringDeserializer;
import org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringSerializer;
import org.apache.kafka.streams.StreamsConfig;
import org.apache.kafka.streams.Topology;
import org.apache.kafka.streams.TopologyTestDriver;
import org.apache.kafka.streams.processor.api.Processor;
import org.apache.kafka.streams.processor.api.ProcessorContext;
import org.apache.kafka.streams.processor.api.Record;
import org.apache.kafka.streams.state.KeyValueStore;
import org.apache.kafka.streams.state.Stores;
import org.apache.kafka.streams.test.TestRecord;

import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Properties;

public class GlobalStoreHeadersRepro {

    static final List<String> SEEN = new ArrayList<>();

    static final class RecordingDeserializer implements Deserializer<String> {
        @Override
        public String deserialize(String topic, byte[] data) {
            SEEN.add("called without headers");
            return data == null ? null : new String(data, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        }

        @Override
        public String deserialize(String topic, Headers headers, byte[] data) {
            var origin = headers == null ? null : headers.lastHeader("origin");
            SEEN.add(origin == null ? "empty headers" : "origin=" + new String(origin.value(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
            return data == null ? null : new String(data, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        }
    }

    static Serde<String> recordingSerde() {
        return Serdes.serdeFrom(new StringSerializer(), new RecordingDeserializer());
    }

    static RecordHeaders origin(String value) {
        var headers = new RecordHeaders();
        headers.add("origin", value.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
        return headers;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        var topology = new Topology();
        topology.addGlobalStore(
                Stores.keyValueStoreBuilder(Stores.inMemoryKeyValueStore("global-store"), Serdes.String(),
                        recordingSerde()).withLoggingDisabled(),
                "global-source", new StringDeserializer(), new StringDeserializer(), "global-topic",
                "global-processor", () -> new Processor<String, String, Void, Void>() {
                    private KeyValueStore<String, String> store;

                    @Override
                    public void init(ProcessorContext<Void, Void> context) {
                        store = context.getStateStore("global-store");
                    }

                    @Override
                    public void process(Record<String, String> record) {
                        store.put(record.key(), record.value());
                    }
                });
        topology.addSource("stream-source", new StringDeserializer(), new StringDeserializer(), "stream-topic");
        topology.addProcessor("reader", () -> new Processor<String, String, Void, Void>() {
            private KeyValueStore<String, String> globalStore;
            private KeyValueStore<String, String> taskStore;

            @Override
            public void init(ProcessorContext<Void, Void> context) {
                globalStore = context.getStateStore("global-store");
                taskStore = context.getStateStore("task-store");
            }

            @Override
            public void process(Record<String, String> record) {
                taskStore.put("k", "task-value");
                SEEN.clear();
                taskStore.get("k");
                System.out.println("stream thread, task store read: " + SEEN);
                SEEN.clear();
                globalStore.get("k");
                System.out.println("stream thread, global store read: " + SEEN);
            }
        }, "stream-source");
        topology.addStateStore(
                Stores.keyValueStoreBuilder(Stores.inMemoryKeyValueStore("task-store"), Serdes.String(),
                        recordingSerde()).withLoggingDisabled(),
                "reader");

        var props = new Properties();
        props.put(StreamsConfig.APPLICATION_ID_CONFIG, "global-store-headers-repro");
        props.put(StreamsConfig.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG, "dummy:1234");

        try (var driver = new TopologyTestDriver(topology, props)) {
            var globalInput = driver.createInputTopic("global-topic", new StringSerializer(), new StringSerializer());
            var streamInput = driver.createInputTopic("stream-topic", new StringSerializer(), new StringSerializer());

            globalInput.pipeInput(new TestRecord<>("k", "global-value", origin("global-record")));
            System.out.println("piped the stream record with origin=stream-record");
            streamInput.pipeInput(new TestRecord<>("x", "y", origin("stream-record")));

            SEEN.clear();
            KeyValueStore<String, String> queried = driver.getKeyValueStore("global-store");
            queried.get("k");
            System.out.println("interactive query, global store read: " + SEEN);
        }
    }
}

What I think could be done: give reads from outside the global thread (stream task processors and interactive queries) either empty headers or the headers of the reading task's current record. Not sure which one fits best. Resetting the global processor context's record context after each update would also stop the headers from leaking past the update.

fields.description:
`partitioner.rack.aware` allows user to adjust the route to try the rack as much as possible. However, it is hard to observe the "miss" from client side since we didn't add any metrics for that.

Since the rack is used to save money, the unit of metrics should be bytes. It should record the size of produce requests sent to brokers whose rack differs from `client.rack`. 

This is useful even without `partitioner.rack.aware`, as users can see the cross-rack traffic before and after enabling it.

fields.description:
h3. Problem

Since KIP-966, the broker and the controller use an effective min ISR of min(min.insync.replicas, replica count):
* Broker: {{Partition#effectiveMinIsr}}. It drives the acks=all produce check and the UnderMinIsr/AtMinIsr metrics.
* Controller: {{ReplicationControlManager#getTopicEffectiveMinIsr}}.

KIP-966 states that this requirement "is not guarded by any feature flags/Metadata version", so it applies whether or not ELR is enabled.

{{TopicCommand}} still compares the ISR size against the raw configured {{min.insync.replicas}}. For any topic whose {{min.insync.replicas}} is larger than its replication factor:
* {{--under-min-isr-partitions}} lists partitions that the broker treats as healthy (at min ISR), and acks=all writes to them succeed.
* {{--at-min-isr-partitions}} does not list them, although the broker counts them as at min ISR.

Nothing prevents such a topic from existing:
* Topic creation does not check min.insync.replicas against the replication factor.
* A topic can also inherit a cluster or broker default that is higher than its replication factor.

As a result, operators who follow the CLI open incidents for partitions that are not affected.

h3. Steps to reproduce

Environment: Apache Kafka 4.3.1 and 4.2.2, official {{apache/kafka}} Docker images, 3 KRaft nodes (combined broker+controller), PLAINTEXT. Newly formatted, so {{eligible.leader.replicas.version}} is finalized at 1.

{code}
bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 --create --topic minisr-gt-rf --partitions 1 --replication-factor 2 --config min.insync.replicas=3
bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 --describe --under-min-isr-partitions
bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 --describe --at-min-isr-partitions
echo m1 | bin/kafka-console-producer.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 --topic minisr-gt-rf --command-property acks=all
bin/kafka-get-offsets.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 --topic minisr-gt-rf --time -1
{code}

*Actual* (4.3.1; 4.2.2 is identical apart from the leader id)
* {{--under-min-isr-partitions}} prints {{Topic: minisr-gt-rf Partition: 0 Leader: 3 Replicas: 3,1 Isr: 3,1 Elr: LastKnownElr:}}
* {{--at-min-isr-partitions}} prints nothing.
* The acks=all produce succeeds (exit code 0), and {{kafka-get-offsets}} returns {{minisr-gt-rf:0:1}}.
* On the leader broker:
** {{kafka.server:type=ReplicaManager,name=UnderMinIsrPartitionCount}} stays 0.
** {{kafka.server:type=ReplicaManager,name=AtMinIsrPartitionCount}} goes from 0 to 1.
** {{kafka.cluster:type=Partition,name=UnderMinIsr,topic=minisr-gt-rf,partition=0}} = 0 and {{...name=AtMinIsr,...}} = 1.

*Same result with ELR disabled*
{code}
bin/kafka-features.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 downgrade --feature eligible.leader.replicas.version=0
bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 --create --topic rf1-minisr2 --partitions 1 --replication-factor 1 --config min.insync.replicas=2
{code}
* {{--under-min-isr-partitions}} lists {{rf1-minisr2}} partition 0 ({{Replicas: 1 Isr: 1}}), and {{--at-min-isr-partitions}} does not.
* The acks=all produce succeeds, and the offset advances to 1.
* On the leader, {{UnderMinIsr}} = 0, {{AtMinIsr}} = 1, and {{UnderMinIsrPartitionCount}} stays 0.

*Expected*
The CLI agrees with the broker: the partition is not listed by {{--under-min-isr-partitions}} and is listed by {{--at-min-isr-partitions}}.

h3. Cause

{{tools/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/tools/TopicCommand.java}} ({{PartitionDescription}}, 4.3 branch around L314-327):
{code:java}
int minIsrCount() {
    return Integer.parseInt(config.get(TopicConfig.MIN_IN_SYNC_REPLICAS_CONFIG).value());
}
boolean isUnderMinIsr() {
    return !hasLeader() || info.isr().size() < minIsrCount();
}
boolean isAtMinIsrPartitions() {
    return minIsrCount() == info.isr().size();
}
{code}
The option help (around L778-779) also says "isr count is less than the configured minimum".
The same code and help text are unchanged in the 4.4 branch and on trunk (L314-332, L779-781).

{{core/src/main/scala/kafka/cluster/Partition.scala}} (4.3 branch around L246-248; the same code is at L391-393 in 4.1 and identical in 3.9/4.0):
{code:scala}
private def effectiveMinIsr(leaderLog: UnifiedLog): Int = {
  leaderLog.config.minInSyncReplicas.min(remoteReplicasMap.size + 1)
}
{code}
It is used by {{isUnderMinIsr}}, {{isAtMinIsr}}, the acks=all completion check and {{appendRecordsToLeader}}. None of these depend on ELR.

{{metadata/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/controller/ReplicationControlManager.java}} ({{getTopicEffectiveMinIsr}}, 4.3 branch around L2463-2468) applies the same cap on the controller with {{Math.min(currentMinIsr, replicationFactor)}}.

* Compute the same effective value in {{TopicCommand}}, e.g. {{Math.min(configured, info.replicas().size())}}, and use it in {{isUnderMinIsr()}} and {{isAtMinIsrPartitions()}}.
* Update the help text of both options ("less than / equal to the configured minimum") to say the effective minimum (min of {{min.insync.replicas}} and the replication factor).

* KIP-1372 / KAFKA-19726 (under discussion): would reject new {{min.insync.replicas}} > replication factor configs. The CLI fix is still needed because:
** Existing topics keep the mismatch.
** Topics can fall back to a cluster or broker default above their replication factor (KIP-1372 keeps DELETE allowed).

* KIP-351 / KAFKA-7236: added {{--under-min-isr-partitions}} before the broker-side cap existed.
* KAFKA-4680 (open): {{min.insync.replicas}} can be set higher than the replication factor. It dates from when such writes were rejected. Since the effective-min-ISR cap, they are accepted.
* KAFKA-8695 (resolved as a duplicate of KAFKA-4680): UnderReplicated and UnderMinIsr metrics diverge when the configuration is inconsistent.

renderedFields.description:
Problem

Since KIP-966, the broker and the controller use an effective min ISR of min(min.insync.replicas, replica count):

  • Broker: Partition#effectiveMinIsr. It drives the acks=all produce check and the UnderMinIsr/AtMinIsr metrics.
  • Controller: ReplicationControlManager#getTopicEffectiveMinIsr.

KIP-966 states that this requirement "is not guarded by any feature flags/Metadata version", so it applies whether or not ELR is enabled.

TopicCommand still compares the ISR size against the raw configured min.insync.replicas. For any topic whose min.insync.replicas is larger than its replication factor:

  • --under-min-isr-partitions lists partitions that the broker treats as healthy (at min ISR), and acks=all writes to them succeed.
  • --at-min-isr-partitions does not list them, although the broker counts them as at min ISR.

Nothing prevents such a topic from existing:

  • Topic creation does not check min.insync.replicas against the replication factor.
  • A topic can also inherit a cluster or broker default that is higher than its replication factor.

As a result, operators who follow the CLI open incidents for partitions that are not affected.

Steps to reproduce

Environment: Apache Kafka 4.3.1 and 4.2.2, official apache/kafka Docker images, 3 KRaft nodes (combined broker+controller), PLAINTEXT. Newly formatted, so eligible.leader.replicas.version is finalized at 1.

bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 --create --topic minisr-gt-rf --partitions 1 --replication-factor 2 --config min.insync.replicas=3
bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 --describe --under-min-isr-partitions
bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 --describe --at-min-isr-partitions
echo m1 | bin/kafka-console-producer.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 --topic minisr-gt-rf --command-property acks=all
bin/kafka-get-offsets.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 --topic minisr-gt-rf --time -1

Actual (4.3.1; 4.2.2 is identical apart from the leader id)

  • --under-min-isr-partitions prints Topic: minisr-gt-rf Partition: 0 Leader: 3 Replicas: 3,1 Isr: 3,1 Elr: LastKnownElr:
  • --at-min-isr-partitions prints nothing.
  • The acks=all produce succeeds (exit code 0), and kafka-get-offsets returns minisr-gt-rf:0:1.
  • On the leader broker:
    • kafka.server:type=ReplicaManager,name=UnderMinIsrPartitionCount stays 0.
    • kafka.server:type=ReplicaManager,name=AtMinIsrPartitionCount goes from 0 to 1.
    • kafka.cluster:type=Partition,name=UnderMinIsr,topic=minisr-gt-rf,partition=0 = 0 and ...name=AtMinIsr,... = 1.

Same result with ELR disabled

bin/kafka-features.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 downgrade --feature eligible.leader.replicas.version=0
bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:19092 --create --topic rf1-minisr2 --partitions 1 --replication-factor 1 --config min.insync.replicas=2
  • -under-min-isr-partitions lists rf1-minisr2 partition 0 (Replicas: 1 Isr: 1), and -at-min-isr-partitions does not.
  • The acks=all produce succeeds, and the offset advances to 1.
  • On the leader, UnderMinIsr = 0, AtMinIsr = 1, and UnderMinIsrPartitionCount stays 0.

Expected
The CLI agrees with the broker: the partition is not listed by -under-min-isr-partitions and is listed by -at-min-isr-partitions.

Cause

tools/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/tools/TopicCommand.java (PartitionDescription, 4.3 branch around L314-327):

int minIsrCount() {
    return Integer.parseInt(config.get(TopicConfig.MIN_IN_SYNC_REPLICAS_CONFIG).value());
}
boolean isUnderMinIsr() {
    return !hasLeader() || info.isr().size() < minIsrCount();
}
boolean isAtMinIsrPartitions() {
    return minIsrCount() == info.isr().size();
}

The option help (around L778-779) also says "isr count is less than the configured minimum".
The same code and help text are unchanged in the 4.4 branch and on trunk (L314-332, L779-781).

core/src/main/scala/kafka/cluster/Partition.scala (4.3 branch around L246-248; the same code is at L391-393 in 4.1 and identical in 3.9/4.0):

private def effectiveMinIsr(leaderLog: UnifiedLog): Int = {
  leaderLog.config.minInSyncReplicas.min(remoteReplicasMap.size + 1)
}

It is used by isUnderMinIsr, isAtMinIsr, the acks=all completion check and appendRecordsToLeader. None of these depend on ELR.

metadata/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/controller/ReplicationControlManager.java (getTopicEffectiveMinIsr, 4.3 branch around L2463-2468) applies the same cap on the controller with Math.min(currentMinIsr, replicationFactor).

Proposed fix

  • Compute the same effective value in TopicCommand, e.g. Math.min(configured, info.replicas().size()), and use it in isUnderMinIsr() and isAtMinIsrPartitions().
  • Update the help text of both options ("less than / equal to the configured minimum") to say the effective minimum (min of min.insync.replicas and the replication factor).
  • Optionally, show the effective value next to the configured one in --describe output when they differ.
  • Add tests in TopicCommandTest for a topic with min.insync.replicas > replication factor.

Related

  • KIP-966 (Eligible Leader Replicas): introduced the effective min ISR. The KIP notes that it is not gated by a feature flag or metadata version.
  • KIP-1372 / KAFKA-19726 (under discussion): would reject new min.insync.replicas > replication factor configs. The CLI fix is still needed because:
    • Existing topics keep the mismatch.
    • Topics can fall back to a cluster or broker default above their replication factor (KIP-1372 keeps DELETE allowed).
    • Topic creation itself does not validate min.insync.replicas against the replication factor today.
  • KIP-351 / KAFKA-7236: added --under-min-isr-partitions before the broker-side cap existed.
  • KAFKA-4680 (open): min.insync.replicas can be set higher than the replication factor. It dates from when such writes were rejected. Since the effective-min-ISR cap, they are accepted.
  • KAFKA-8695 (resolved as a duplicate of KAFKA-4680): UnderReplicated and UnderMinIsr metrics diverge when the configuration is inconsistent.
  • KAFKA-20235 (open): expose EffectiveMinIsr as a partition metric. Complementary to this issue, since operators could then compare the CLI against the effective value.

To support "bumpLeaderEpoch" RPC in the future, we should add a "leaderEpoch" field in PartitionChangeRecord, and move the leader epoch calculation logic from currently each node calculate the leader epoch when replying PartitionChangeRecord in PartitionRegistration class, to each time the PartitionChangeRecord creates, and each node only needs to take the leaderEpoch in the PartitionChangeRecord.

 

We should also consider the backward compatibility in this change.

fields.description:
When the DLQ flow is enabled for a share group (KIP-1191), records whose delivery
count reaches the limit are moved to ARCHIVING on the normal release path so they
are written to the DLQ topic (InFlightState.tryUpdateState with dlqSupportEnabled=true).

However, the rollback path in InFlightState.completeStateTransition(false) - taken
when a two-phase state transition fails (e.g. the persister write fails) and the
acquisition lock has expired - archives the records directly:

    state = previousState.deliveryCount() >= rollbackState.maxDeliveryCount ?
        RecordState.ARCHIVED : RecordState.AVAILABLE;

This bypasses the DLQ flow entirely: records that should have been dead-lettered are
silently archived and never appear in the DLQ topic. Two related inconsistencies:
1. ARCHIVING (normal path) vs ARCHIVED (rollback path) for the same limit-reached
   condition.
2. The normal path evaluates the limit with the delivery count including the current
   delivery, while the rollback path uses previousState.deliveryCount() - the counts
   differ by one.

Note that completeStateTransition(boolean) has no access to the dlqSupportEnabled
flag, so the rollback path cannot currently reach ARCHIVING.

Reproduction: new unit test InFlightStateTest
(testFailedStateTransitionWithExpiredLockDeadLettersWhenDlqSupported) fails on
trunk and passes with the fix.

Proposed fix: thread the DLQ-support flag through the rollback path, mirroring the
normal transition path, and start the DLQ flow for batches that move to ARCHIVING
in both the local rollback and the persister-failure paths.

Two test scenarios (step 5 in the reproduction) verify:
- normal release path at the limit moves records to ARCHIVING (baseline)
- rollback with expired lock at the limit moves records to ARCHIVING when DLQ is
  enabled, and to ARCHIVED when disabled
fields.summary: Failed state-transition rollback bypasses DLQ when delivery count limit is reached

comments.body: This was deliberately avoided as a persister fail => a 5 time call to persister with exponential backoff failed. Now with DLQ again, the first step is ARCHIVING which requires a persister write. This too has good chance of failing (same partition key, so same broker). Hence the decision was taken to not stall the in-flight records queue over this.

Closing [#23995|https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23995] as the rollback behavior is intentional: when the persister has already failed after retries, routing through ARCHIVING would likely hit the same failure and stall the in-flight queue. Keeping this issue open for the record. Thanks Sushant for the clarification.

fields.description:
When the group coordinator defers computing a new target assignment for a streams group because the configured assignment interval has not elapsed, it returns the {{ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED}} status in the heartbeat response. The member keeps its current assignment in this case. {{StreamsMembershipManager}}, however, treats {{ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED}} like {{MISSING_SOURCE_TOPICS}}, {{MISSING_INTERNAL_TOPICS}} and {{INCORRECTLY_PARTITIONED_TOPICS}} and reports the group as not ready. The membership manager re-reconciles the unchanged tasks with {{isGroupReady=false}}, and {{StreamThread}} stops processing, committing and punctuating all tasks it owns until a later heartbeat no longer carries the status, which takes up to one heartbeat interval (5 seconds by default).

This happens both when the heartbeat response carries no task changes and when the broker echoes the unchanged assignment after the member reports its owned tasks.

{{ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED}} should not turn a ready member into a not-ready one. It should keep the readiness of the previous target assignment, so that a member that has not been ready yet (e.g., during the initial rebalance delay of a new group) still does not enter {{RUNNING}} with an empty assignment, while a ready member keeps processing. Missing or incorrectly partitioned topics should still mark the group as not ready, also when reported together with {{ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED}}.
